title: Chemical Engineering Thermodynamics
description: This syllabus treats thermodynamics as the bridge between process equipment, property methods, phase behavior, and reaction equilibrium. It is suitable for a core chemical engineering course after material and energy balances and before separations, reactors, and process design.

topics.title: Thermodynamic Modeling for Chemical Engineering Systems
topics.description: Frame chemical engineering thermodynamics as property modeling, energy accounting, equilibrium prediction, and process decision-making.

children.title: Thermodynamic Vocabulary and Scope
children.description: This subtopic establishes the language used to turn physical processes into solvable thermodynamic models.

children.title: System, surroundings, boundary, closed system, open system, isolated system
State, process, path, cycle, equilibrium state, and steady state
Intensive property, extensive property, specific property, and molar property
Simple compressible substance, phase, component, and degree of freedom
Modeling Assumptions and Sign Conventions
children.description: Students learn to state assumptions clearly so calculations are interpretable and reproducible.

children.title: Heat sign convention, work sign convention, shaft work, boundary work, and flow work
Steady versus transient operation
Adiabatic, isothermal, isobaric, isochoric, reversible, irreversible, and internally reversible processes
Neglecting kinetic energy, potential energy, pressure drop, or heat loss when justified
Property Needs in Chemical Processes
children.description: The point is to connect thermodynamics to process equipment, separations, reactors, and property packages.

children.title: Temperature, pressure, composition, phase fraction, enthalpy, entropy, and Gibbs energy
Property database, property correlation, equation of state, and activity-coefficient model
Process simulator property package and method selection
Energy balance, phase equilibrium, and reaction equilibrium as linked calculations

topics.title: First Law for Closed Systems
topics.description: Apply energy conservation to non-flow systems with heat, work, internal energy, and phase change.

children.title: Closed-System Energy Balance
children.description: This subtopic teaches the basic accounting rule for energy in non-flow systems.

children.title: Internal energy change, heat transfer, and work transfer
Boundary work integral and P-V work
Constant-volume, constant-pressure, isothermal, and adiabatic processes
Rigid tank, piston-cylinder device, spring-loaded piston, and two-phase vessel
Heat Capacity and Sensible Energy
children.description: Students learn how temperature changes translate into internal-energy and enthalpy changes.

children.title: Constant-volume heat capacity and constant-pressure heat capacity
Ideal-gas heat-capacity functions and temperature dependence
Sensible heat, latent heat, and reference state
Calorimetry-style calculations and tabulated property changes
Phase Change in Closed Systems
children.description: This section connects energy balances to vaporization, condensation, melting, and quality.

children.title: Saturated liquid, saturated vapor, compressed liquid, superheated vapor, and two-phase mixture
Quality, latent heat, internal energy of vaporization, and enthalpy of vaporization
Heating at fixed volume versus heating at fixed pressure
Mass fraction vaporized and final-state determination

topics.title: First Law for Open Systems and Flow Processes
topics.description: Analyze steady and unsteady flow devices using enthalpy, shaft work, flow work, kinetic energy, and potential energy.

children.title: Steady-Flow Energy Equation
children.description: The goal is to analyze real process equipment using enthalpy and flow work.

children.title: Mass flow rate, control volume, inlet, outlet, and steady-state balance
Enthalpy, shaft work, heat transfer, kinetic energy, and potential energy terms
Turbine, compressor, pump, nozzle, diffuser, heat exchanger, and throttling valve
Single-inlet/single-outlet and multiple-stream control volumes
Unsteady Flow and Transient Balances
children.description: Students learn how tanks, filling operations, and discharge processes differ from steady equipment.

children.title: Accumulation of mass and energy
Charging, discharging, blowdown, and startup/shutdown operations
Uniform-state and uniform-flow approximations
Transient mixing tank and pressure vessel examples
Chemical Engineering Unit Applications
children.description: This subtopic gives the first law a process-engineering context.

children.title: Steam generation, condensers, evaporators, flash drums, and heat exchangers
Mixing of ideal gases and liquid streams
Joule-Thomson throttling and valve calculations
Adiabatic flame temperature as an energy-balance extension

topics.title: Pure-Substance Properties and Property Data
topics.description: Use tables, diagrams, databases, and correlations to evaluate thermodynamic states of pure substances.

children.title: Phase Diagrams and State Location
children.description: Students learn to identify the physical state before calculating properties.

children.title: P-v, T-v, P-T, T-s, and H-s diagrams
Triple point, critical point, saturation dome, and supercritical region
Compressed liquid, subcooled liquid, saturated mixture, superheated vapor
Quality lines, vapor pressure curve, and phase boundary
Property Tables and Databases
children.description: The point is to use data sources accurately and recognize interpolation limits.

children.title: Saturation tables, superheated-vapor tables, compressed-liquid tables
Interpolation in temperature, pressure, and quality
Reference states and consistency across data sources
NIST Chemistry WebBook, steam tables, and refrigerant tables
Correlations for Pure-Substance Properties
children.description: Students learn when tabulated data can be replaced by correlations.

children.title: Antoine equation, vapor-pressure correlations, and normal boiling point
Heat-capacity polynomials and enthalpy departure
Clapeyron and Clausius-Clapeyron equations
Acentric factor and corresponding-states properties

topics.title: Equations of State and Real-Fluid Behavior
topics.description: Model real gases and fluids using virial, cubic, corresponding-states, and departure-function methods.

children.title: Ideal Gas and Virial Models
children.description: This section starts with simple models and shows where real-gas corrections enter.

children.title: Ideal-gas law, compressibility factor, and Z chart
Second virial coefficient, third virial coefficient, and density expansions
Boyle temperature and low-pressure behavior
Mixture virial coefficients and combining rules
Cubic Equations of State
children.description: Students learn widely used process models for vapor-liquid and real-fluid calculations.

children.title: Van der Waals, Redlich-Kwong, Soave-Redlich-Kwong, and Peng-Robinson equations
Attraction parameter, co-volume parameter, alpha function, and acentric factor
Cubic roots, liquid root, vapor root, and metastable roots
Critical constants, binary interaction parameter, and mixing rules
Departure and Residual Properties
children.description: The goal is to calculate real-fluid property changes relative to ideal-gas reference behavior.

children.title: Residual enthalpy, residual entropy, residual Gibbs energy, and residual volume
Departure functions from equations of state
Ideal-gas contribution plus residual contribution
Fugacity coefficient from equation-of-state models

topics.title: Second Law, Entropy, and Irreversibility
topics.description: Use entropy balances and the second law to judge feasibility, losses, and process direction.

children.title: Entropy Balance
children.description: Students learn the second-law accounting equation for process feasibility and losses.

children.title: Entropy transfer with heat, entropy generation, and entropy accumulation
Closed-system entropy balance and control-volume entropy balance
Reversible heat transfer and Clausius inequality
Entropy changes for ideal gases, liquids, solids, and phase changes
Irreversibility in Process Equipment
children.description: This subtopic helps students identify why real equipment cannot reach ideal performance.

children.title: Friction, pressure drop, finite-temperature heat transfer, mixing, throttling, and chemical reaction
Isentropic turbine, isentropic compressor, and isentropic efficiency
Adiabatic throttling and Joule-Thomson effect
Minimum work, lost work, and entropy generation minimization
Second-Law Feasibility Tests
children.description: The point is to determine whether a proposed process can occur as written.

children.title: Entropy generation greater than or equal to zero
Heat engine, refrigerator, and heat pump limits
Carnot efficiency and coefficient of performance
Reversibility, impossibility, and process direction

topics.title: Exergy, Availability, and Process Efficiency
topics.description: Quantify useful work potential and destroyed work in process equipment and cycles.

children.title: Exergy Concepts
children.description: Exergy translates thermodynamics into useful-work potential relative to an environment.

children.title: Dead state, restricted dead state, environment temperature and pressure
Physical exergy, chemical exergy, flow exergy, and nonflow exergy
Availability, useful work, reversible work, and lost work
Gouy-Stodola theorem and exergy destruction
Exergy Balances for Equipment
children.description: Students learn to locate inefficiency across individual process units.

children.title: Control-volume exergy balance
Turbine, compressor, pump, heat exchanger, valve, and reactor exergy terms
Exergy transfer by heat, work, and mass flow
Second-law efficiency and rational efficiency
Process-Level Exergy Analysis
children.description: This subtopic connects equipment calculations to process improvement decisions.

children.title: Pinch-like thinking, heat recovery, and wasted work potential
Combustion, separation, mixing, and reaction irreversibility
Exergy destruction map and process bottleneck
Trade-offs between efficiency, cost, complexity, and safety

topics.title: Power, Refrigeration, Heat Pump, and Liquefaction Cycles
topics.description: Apply first-law and second-law tools to thermal cycles relevant to chemical and energy systems.

children.title: Power Cycles
children.description: Students apply thermodynamic balances to cycles that convert heat into work.

children.title: Carnot cycle, Rankine cycle, reheat, regeneration, and boiler/condenser roles
Brayton cycle, pressure ratio, compressor work, and turbine work
Thermal efficiency, back work ratio, and net work
Steam power, gas turbine, and combined-cycle concepts
Refrigeration and Heat Pump Cycles
children.description: The gist is to calculate how work moves heat from low temperature to high temperature.

children.title: Vapor-compression refrigeration cycle
Evaporator, compressor, condenser, expansion valve, and refrigerant
Coefficient of performance, superheating, subcooling, and compressor efficiency
Absorption refrigeration and working-fluid pairs
Liquefaction and Cryogenic Processes
children.description: Chemical engineers use thermodynamics to design low-temperature separation and gas-processing systems.

children.title: Joule-Thomson expansion, inversion temperature, and throttling
Linde cycle, Claude cycle, and cascade refrigeration
Flash separation after throttling
Natural gas processing, air separation, and cryogenic safety

topics.title: Thermodynamic Property Relations and Maxwell Relations
topics.description: Derive and use property identities that connect measurable variables to U, H, A, G, S, P, V, and T.

children.title: Fundamental Equations and Potentials
children.description: This subtopic shows how U, H, A, and G organize thermodynamic information.

children.title: Internal energy U, enthalpy H, Helmholtz energy A, and Gibbs energy G
Natural variables and exact differentials
Legendre transforms and thermodynamic potentials
Chemical potential as partial molar Gibbs energy
Maxwell Relations and Measurable Derivatives
children.description: Students learn to replace hard-to-measure derivatives with measurable property relationships.

children.title: Maxwell relations from exact differentials
Thermal expansion coefficient, isothermal compressibility, and heat capacities
Cyclic rule, reciprocity relation, and chain rule for partial derivatives
Entropy and enthalpy changes from P-V-T data
Useful Property Identities
children.description: The goal is practical calculation of property changes for real substances.

children.title: Gibbs-Helmholtz equation
Clapeyron equation and phase-transition slope
Residual-property identities
Heat-capacity relationships and speed-of-sound connections

topics.title: Mixture Properties, Partial Molar Quantities, and Excess Properties
topics.description: Extend thermodynamics from pure fluids to mixtures using chemical potential, partial molar properties, residual properties, and excess functions.

children.title: Partial Molar Properties
children.description: Students learn how each component contributes to mixture properties in a composition-dependent way.

children.title: Partial molar volume, partial molar enthalpy, partial molar entropy, and partial molar Gibbs energy
Chemical potential and composition derivatives
Gibbs-Duhem equation and consistency constraints
Tangent-intercept method and apparent molar properties
Ideal and Nonideal Mixtures
children.description: This subtopic distinguishes mixture models that ignore interactions from models that account for them.

children.title: Ideal-gas mixture, ideal solution, Raoult's law, and Henry's law
Excess Gibbs energy, excess enthalpy, excess entropy, and excess volume
Activity, activity coefficient, fugacity, and fugacity coefficient
Azeotrope, miscibility gap, and nonideal mixing behavior
Residual Properties of Mixtures
children.description: The point is to compute real-fluid mixture properties using equations of state.

children.title: Mixture residual Gibbs energy, residual enthalpy, and residual entropy
Mixing rules, binary interaction parameter, and pseudo-critical properties
Fugacity coefficients in mixtures
Property package selection for hydrocarbon, polar, and associating systems

topics.title: Fugacity, Chemical Potential, and Equilibrium Criteria
topics.description: Use fugacity and chemical potential to express equilibrium in real-fluid systems.

children.title: Chemical Potential as an Equilibrium Tool
children.description: Chemical potential provides a single language for phase, chemical, and material equilibrium.

children.title: Chemical potential, molar Gibbs energy, and partial molar Gibbs energy
Equilibrium as equal chemical potential across phases
Stability, spontaneity, and Gibbs energy minimization
Temperature, pressure, and composition effects on chemical potential
Fugacity and Fugacity Coefficients
children.description: Students learn why fugacity replaces pressure for real gases and real fluids.

children.title: Fugacity, fugacity coefficient, standard state, and reference state
Pure-component fugacity from P-V-T data
Mixture fugacity and component fugacity
Equation-of-state calculation of fugacity coefficient
Equilibrium Criteria Across Systems
children.description: The goal is to set up the correct equality before solving any numerical problem.

children.title: VLE criterion, LLE criterion, SLE criterion, and vapor-solid equilibrium criterion
Phi-phi, gamma-phi, and gamma-gamma formulations
K-value definition and distribution ratio
Thermodynamic consistency and phase stability checks

topics.title: Phase Equilibria: VLE, LLE, SLE, and Flash Calculations
topics.description: Predict phase splits and compositions for nonreactive mixtures using K-values, activity models, and equations of state.

children.title: Vapor-Liquid Equilibrium
children.description: Students learn the central equilibrium calculation used in distillation, absorption, stripping, and flash processes.

children.title: Bubble point, dew point, relative volatility, and K-value
Raoult's law, modified Raoult's law, Henry's law, and Poynting correction
T-x-y diagram, P-x-y diagram, y-x diagram, and azeotrope
Low-pressure VLE, high-pressure VLE, and equation-of-state VLE
Liquid-Liquid and Solid-Liquid Equilibrium
children.description: This subtopic covers phase splits beyond vapor-liquid behavior.

children.title: Miscibility gap, tie line, plait point, binodal curve, and ternary diagram
Distribution coefficient and extraction equilibrium
Solubility, crystallization, eutectic point, and solid solution
Polymer solution and electrolyte solution considerations
Flash Calculations
children.description: The point is to solve material and equilibrium balances together for phase split and compositions.

children.title: Isothermal flash, adiabatic flash, and pressure-temperature flash
Rachford-Rice equation and vapor fraction
Successive substitution, Newton method, and convergence
Phase stability, initial estimates, and material-balance closure

topics.title: Activity Coefficients and Nonideal Liquid Solutions
topics.description: Model nonideal liquid phases using excess-Gibbs-energy models and composition-dependent activity coefficients.

children.title: Activity-Coefficient Definitions
children.description: Students learn how nonideal liquid behavior enters equilibrium calculations.

children.title: Activity, activity coefficient, standard state, and reference-state convention
Henry's-law standard state versus Raoult's-law standard state
Infinite-dilution activity coefficient
Excess Gibbs energy and gamma model connection
Local-Composition and Empirical Models
children.description: This subtopic gives students the named models used in process simulators and design calculations.

children.title: Margules, van Laar, Wilson, NRTL, UNIQUAC, and UNIFAC
Binary parameters, temperature dependence, and regression from VLE/LLE data
Local composition, molecular size, surface area, and group contribution
Model-selection limits for polar, associating, electrolyte, and polymer systems
Data Regression and Consistency
children.description: The goal is to use experimental data responsibly rather than treating model output as automatically true.

children.title: Parameter estimation, objective function, residuals, and confidence
Gibbs-Duhem consistency and area tests
Azeotrope prediction, LLE split prediction, and extrapolation risk
Comparison against NIST, DECHEMA-style data, and literature data

topics.title: Chemical Reaction and Multireaction Equilibrium
topics.description: Predict equilibrium conversion and composition for reacting systems using Gibbs energy minimization and equilibrium constants.

children.title: Single-Reaction Equilibrium
children.description: Students learn how equilibrium constants connect thermodynamics to reactor composition limits.

children.title: Standard Gibbs energy of reaction, equilibrium constant, and reaction quotient
Extent of reaction, conversion, selectivity, and equilibrium composition
Temperature dependence, van't Hoff equation, and heat of reaction
Pressure effects and inert effects for gas-phase reactions
Multireaction and Multiphase Equilibrium
children.description: This subtopic reflects real processes where several reactions and phases interact.

children.title: Independent reactions, stoichiometric matrix, and reaction coordinates
Gibbs energy minimization and element balances
Simultaneous reaction and phase equilibrium
Gas-solid, gas-liquid, liquid-liquid reactive systems, and precipitation
Process Applications and Equilibrium Limits
children.description: The final section ties reaction equilibrium to process choices and design intuition.

children.title: Ammonia synthesis, steam methane reforming, water-gas shift, esterification, and combustion
Equilibrium conversion versus kinetic limitation
Le Chatelier's principle, temperature choice, pressure choice, and separation coupling
Reactive distillation, recycle, purge, and equilibrium-stage thinking
